The undersigned, acting as incorporator of a corporation under the General Not For Profit Corporation Act of the State of Illinois, does hereby adopt the following Articles of Incorporation:

ARTICLE I – NAME
The name of the corporation shall be Riverbend Legal Aid Society (hereinafter "RLAS" or the "Society").

ARTICLE II – PURPOSE
The Society is organized exclusively for charitable, educational, and scientific purposes, including, for such purposes, the making of distributions to organizations that qualify as exempt organizations under section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code, or the corresponding section of any future federal tax code. The specific purpose of the Society is to provide free civil legal assistance to low-income residents of the greater Rockford metropolitan area, with an emphasis on housing stability, family safety, consumer protection, and access to public benefits.

ARTICLE III – REGISTERED OFFICE AND AGENT
The address of the registered office of the Society is 2143 State Street, Suite 200, Rockford, Illinois 61104. The name of the registered agent at such address is Margaret H. Kowalski.

ARTICLE IV – DIRECTORS
The affairs of the Society shall be managed by a Board of Directors consisting of no fewer than five and no more than fifteen members. The initial Board of Directors shall consist of the individuals named in Section 2 of this Certificate.

ARTICLE V – DISSOLUTION
Upon the dissolution of the Society, assets shall be distributed for one or more exempt purposes within the meaning of section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code, or shall be distributed to the federal government, or to a state or local government, for a public purpose.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned has executed these Articles of Incorporation this 15th day of April, 2019.

I. CALL TO ORDER
Reverend Okafor called the meeting to order at 9:03 a.m. A quorum was present.

II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES
The minutes of the 2019-04-15 regular meeting were distributed in advance. Motion to approve the minutes as submitted was made by Dr. Raman and seconded by Mr. Espinoza. VOTE: Unanimous. RESULT: Motion carried.

III. EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR’S REPORT
Ms. Vasquez reported on the first six weeks of her tenure. She reviewed the status of the Society’s lease at 2140 Commerce Street, noting that the landlord had agreed to extend the term through 2024-06-30 with a renewal option. She also reported that the Society’s bank accounts had been consolidated from two legacy accounts into a single operating account at Merchants & Farmers Bank, effective 2019-05-20.

Ms. Vasquez then introduced the topic of the Society’s service expansion. She stated that, based on her initial review of intake data and community partner conversations, the Society should consider establishing a dedicated tenant rights clinic. She noted that eviction filings in the county had increased by 18% over the prior year and that current pro bono coverage for landlord-tenant matters was inconsistent.

IV. DISCUSSION: POTENTIAL TENANT RIGHTS CLINIC
Mr. Espinoza asked about the anticipated start-up costs. Ms. Vasquez estimated that a part-time staff attorney, a paralegal, and limited interpretation services could be added for approximately $145,000 in the first year, with space and administrative overhead shared with existing operations. Mr. Whitfield noted that the current budget had a contingency reserve of $60,000 and suggested that a grant application could cover the remainder.

Dr. Raman moved that the Board authorize the Executive Director to prepare a formal feasibility study and grant application for a tenant rights clinic, to be presented at the next regular meeting. The motion was seconded by Mr. Whitfield.

Discussion followed on the scope of the clinic. Ms. Vasquez proposed that the clinic focus on eviction defense, habitability claims, and security deposit disputes, and that it operate two evenings per week and one Saturday per month. The Board agreed that this scope was appropriate for an initial phase.

VOTE: Unanimous. RESULT: Motion carried.

V. RESOLUTION NO. 2019-03: AUTHORIZATION TO PURSUE TENANT RIGHTS CLINIC FEASIBILITY

WHEREAS, the Riverbend Legal Aid Society is committed to expanding access to civil legal services for low-income residents; and

WHEREAS, data from the county court system indicates a rising number of eviction filings and a gap in available legal assistance for tenant respondents; and

WHEREAS, the Board has determined that a dedicated tenant rights clinic could address this gap; and

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED:

1. That the Executive Director is authorized to conduct a feasibility study for the establishment of a tenant rights clinic.
2. That the Executive Director is authorized to prepare and submit grant applications to fund the clinic’s first year of operations.
3. That the Executive Director shall report on the feasibility study and grant status at the next regular Board meeting.

documents.content:
The undersigned, acting as incorporator of a corporation under the General Not For Profit Corporation Act of the State of Illinois, does hereby adopt the following Articles of Incorporation:

ARTICLE I – NAME
The name of the corporation shall be Riverbend Legal Aid Society (hereinafter "RLAS" or the "Society").

ARTICLE II – PURPOSE
The Society is organized exclusively for charitable, educational, and scientific purposes, including, for such purposes, the making of distributions to organizations that qualify as exempt organizations under section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code, or the corresponding section of any future federal tax code. The specific purpose of the Society is to provide free civil legal assistance to low-income residents of the greater Rockford metropolitan area, with an emphasis on housing stability, family safety, consumer protection, and access to public benefits.

ARTICLE III – REGISTERED OFFICE AND AGENT
The address of the registered office of the Society is 2143 State Street, Suite 200, Rockford, Illinois 61104. The name of the registered agent at such address is Margaret H. Kowalski.

ARTICLE IV – DIRECTORS
The affairs of the Society shall be managed by a Board of Directors consisting of no fewer than five and no more than fifteen members. The initial Board of Directors shall consist of the individuals named in Section 2 of this Certificate.

ARTICLE V – DISSOLUTION
Upon the dissolution of the Society, assets shall be distributed for one or more exempt purposes within the meaning of section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code, or shall be distributed to the federal government, or to a state or local government, for a public purpose.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned has executed these Articles of Incorporation this 15th day of April, 2019.

______________________________
Margaret H. Kowalski, Incorporator

Filed with the Illinois Secretary of State on 2019-04-15.

---

RESOLUTION NO. 2019-01
ADOPTED BY THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS
ON 2019-04-15

WHEREAS, the Riverbend Legal Aid Society has been duly incorporated under the laws of the State of Illinois; and

WHEREAS, the Board of Directors desires to formally commence operations of the Society and to authorize the Executive Director to take all necessary actions to establish the Society's administrative infrastructure;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED:

Riverbend Legal Aid Society launch_date 2019-04-15 date. Record status: current.

1. That the Society officially opens its doors for operations on 2019-04-15.
2. That the Executive Director is authorized to open bank accounts, execute leases, hire staff, and enter into contracts necessary for the operation of the Society.
3. That the Executive Director shall report to the Board at each regular meeting on all actions taken pursuant to this resolution.

ADOPTED UNANIMOUSLY by the Board of Directors on 2019-04-15.

CERTIFIED BY:

______________________________
Margaret H. Kowalski, Secretary of the Board

III. EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR’S REPORT
Ms. Vasquez reported on the first six weeks of her tenure. She reviewed the status of the Society’s lease at 2140 Commerce Street, noting that the landlord had agreed to extend the term through 2024-06-30 with a renewal option. She also reported that the Society’s bank accounts had been consolidated from two legacy accounts into a single operating account at Merchants & Farmers Bank, effective 2019-05-20.

Ms. Vasquez then introduced the topic of the Society’s service expansion. She stated that, based on her initial review of intake data and community partner conversations, the Society should consider establishing a dedicated tenant rights clinic. She noted that eviction filings in the county had increased by 18% over the prior year and that current pro bono coverage for landlord-tenant matters was inconsistent.

IV. DISCUSSION: POTENTIAL TENANT RIGHTS CLINIC
Mr. Espinoza asked about the anticipated start-up costs. Ms. Vasquez estimated that a part-time staff attorney, a paralegal, and limited interpretation services could be added for approximately $145,000 in the first year, with space and administrative overhead shared with existing operations. Mr. Whitfield noted that the current budget had a contingency reserve of $60,000 and suggested that a grant application could cover the remainder.

Dr. Raman moved that the Board authorize the Executive Director to prepare a formal feasibility study and grant application for a tenant rights clinic, to be presented at the next regular meeting. The motion was seconded by Mr. Whitfield.

Discussion followed on the scope of the clinic. Ms. Vasquez proposed that the clinic focus on eviction defense, habitability claims, and security deposit disputes, and that it operate two evenings per week and one Saturday per month. The Board agreed that this scope was appropriate for an initial phase.

1. That the Executive Director is authorized to conduct a feasibility study for the establishment of a tenant rights clinic.
2. That the Executive Director is authorized to prepare and submit grant applications to fund the clinic’s first year of operations.
